card_summary: Vizrt, a company, launched Sports Production Bundles. The bundles are for US students. The bundles include Vizrt software and hardware for live sports production, supporting ST 2110 and NMOS standards. This enables students to produce sports content with low latency and variable bitrate.
body_html:
Vizrt has launched sports production bundles designed to enable US students to produce high-quality sports content, mirroring professional broadcast standards. The bundles include Vizrt's graphics and video editing tools, tailored for educational institutions. This launch occurred in the US market, where sports production is a significant sector.

Technical Breakdown

Vizrt's sports production bundles integrate with IP-based infrastructures, adhering to ST 2110 standards for video and AES67 for audio. The bundles utilize NMOS (Networked Media Open Specifications) for device discovery and registration, facilitating streamlined setup and operation. In terms of codecs, the bundles support JPEG XS for low-latency, visually lossless compression, suitable for live sports production. The Vizrt tools also incorporate APIs for integration with third-party systems, such as MAM (Media Asset Management) and playout automation. This allows for a unified workflow, from ingest to delivery, using protocols like SRT (Secure Reliable Transport) for secure video transport.

Operational Impact for Broadcast Engineers

The introduction of Vizrt's sports production bundles affects several workflow steps for broadcast engineers, particularly in educational settings. Engineers must evaluate the bundles' compatibility with existing infrastructure, considering factors like network bandwidth and device support for ST 2110 and NMOS. During the ingest process, engineers will need to ensure that the bundles can handle various video and audio formats, including those using HEVC (H.265) and AV1 codecs. In live production, the bundles' support for low-latency JPEG XS compression will require engineers to adjust their quality settings and bitrate allocation, potentially impacting the overall workflow's latency and bitrate requirements.

Real-World Scenario

A regional TV station in the US, focused on college sports, is considering adopting Vizrt's sports production bundles to enhance their production quality. The station currently uses a mix of SDI and IP-based equipment, with a playout system that supports HLS (HTTP Live Streaming) for OTT delivery. By integrating Vizrt's bundles, the station would need to assess the compatibility of their existing MAM system with the bundles' APIs, ensuring smooth metadata exchange and workflow automation. The station would also need to evaluate the bitrate requirements for their live productions, potentially adjusting their encoding settings to accommodate the low-latency JPEG XS compression, and ensuring that their CDN (Content Delivery Network) can handle the resulting streams.

Industry and Market Signals

Vizrt's launch of sports production bundles for the US educational market signals a shift towards more professional-level tools being made available to students and smaller broadcasters. This move may prompt other vendors to reassess their product offerings and pricing strategies, potentially leading to increased competition in the market for sports production solutions. The adoption of these bundles may also drive demand for IP-based infrastructure and compatible devices, influencing the product roadmaps of manufacturers. Furthermore, the emphasis on low-latency compression and IP-based workflows may lead to increased adoption of standards like ST 2110 and NMOS, as well as codecs like JPEG XS, in the broader broadcast industry.

What to Watch Next

Engineers and technology directors should monitor the development of NMOS and ST 2110 standards, as well as the evolution of codecs like JPEG XS, AV1, and HEVC. The product roadmaps of vendors like Vizrt, as well as other industry players, should be tracked for updates on IP-based workflow support and low-latency compression capabilities. Additionally, the market's shift towards cloud-based and remote production workflows, using protocols like SRT and NDI, will be important to watch, as these trends may influence the design and functionality of future sports production bundles. The emergence of new, more efficient codecs and the growing demand for high-quality, low-latency video will also be crucial to follow, as these factors will shape the future of sports production and broadcasting.

Analysis: Vizrt's bundles support ST 2110, enabling students to produce sports content with professional-grade IP workflows and efficient bitrate management.
